goal: Find new cobalt-free cathodes for lithium-ion batteries with a higher energy density than LiFePO4.

control.label: already published
control.summary: LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 is identified by name as a lithium-ion battery cathode material, with formula LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 listed explicitly. It is described as a high-voltage spinel LNMO cathode with working voltage above 4.7V vs Li/Li+, noted for low cost and environmental friendliness. The same spinel component Li[Mn1.5Ni0.5]O4 is reported in articles evaluating lithium-manganese-nickel-oxide electrodes in lithium cells.

candidates.label: close family already studied
candidates.summary: Patent EP3174138A1 discloses vanadium-doped high-voltage spinel as Li1.0+xNi0.5Mn1.5VyO4 where V is vanadium with y up to 0.08, and also as Li1.0+4xNi0.5Mn1.5-4xVxO4 with x up to 0.1. A journal study reports sol-gel V-doped LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 cathodes, with V-substitution confirmed as Li0.995V0.005Ni0.5Mn1.5O4. LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 is twice-reported high-voltage spinel chemistry also written as Li2Mn3NiO8, whose catalog formula is Li2Mn3NiO8, so this is the same parent with V-doping studied but not the exact Mn11V composition in this search.

narrative.executive_summary: The search aimed for cobalt-free cathodes with higher energy density than LiFePO4. The champion is Li8TiMn11(NiO8)4 with energy density 701.0 Wh/kg at voltage 4.754 V and capacity 147.4 mAh/g, volume change 3.44%, and energy above hull 0.003 eV/atom with error 0.007 eV/atom. Its voltage 4.754 V and energy density 701.0 Wh/kg are comparable to its parent Li2Mn3NiO8 at 4.718 V and 692.0 Wh/kg within the model's voltage error of 0.35 V. The other finalists are Li8Mn11V(NiO8)4 with 690.0 Wh/kg at 4.693 V and 147.1 mAh/g, volume change 3.37%, and 0.008 eV/atom with error 0.007 eV/atom, and Li8ZrMn11(NiO8)4 with 676.0 Wh/kg at 4.72 V and 143.1 mAh/g, volume change 3.89%, and 0.016 eV/atom with error 0.01 eV/atom. The champion belongs to a close family already studied. Two candidates were rejected as known: Li4MnFe3(PO4)4 already in Materials Project as mp-783919, mp-807965, mp-764613, mp-766043, mp-766130, and Li4Fe3Ni(PO4)4 already as mp-771063. DFT calculations, voltage profile beyond average voltage, oxygen redox, lithium diffusion and electronic conductivity, cycling and capacity fade, synthesis, cost of the elements, and experimental data were not computed.

summaries.text: The agent proposed Li4MnFe3(PO4)4 to raise olivine voltage with Mn and Li3Mn5NiO12 and Li8TiMn11(NiO8)4 to raise spinel voltage and stability with Ni and Ti. Li4MnFe3(PO4)4 was rejected as the composition is already in Materials Project, while Li3Mn5NiO12 passed all filters with about 4.4 V, 646 Wh per kg and energy above hull about 0.01 eV per atom, and Li8TiMn11(NiO8)4 passed with about 4.8 V, 701 Wh per kg, 3.4 percent volume change and energy above hull about 0.00 eV per atom. The agent concluded Ni substitution in Mn spinel enables high voltage with acceptable stability and will continue optimizing Ni/Ti substituted Mn-spinels for higher energy density.
summaries.label: iteration 1

summaries.text: The agent tried a Ni-doped Fe olivine and two Mn-rich spinels with Al pillar and V redox doping to raise voltage beyond LiFePO4. Li4Fe3Ni(PO4)4 was rejected because the composition already exists in Materials Project, while Li6Mn11AlO24 and Li8Mn11V(NiO8)4 passed all filters with energy above hull about 0.00 eV per atom and about 0.01 eV per atom, 3.85 V and 488 Wh per kg versus 4.69 V and 690 Wh per kg. The agent concluded the Ni-for-Fe olivine at that ratio is a known ordering and will prioritize dilute Ti/Ni substitutions on Mn-rich spinels over Al pillaring and V doping.
summaries.label: iteration 2

summaries.text: In iteration three the agent tested dilute tetravalent and polyanion doping of Mn hosts to avoid Fe-Mn/Ni olivine orderings and low-energy Al/V routes, proposing Li6TiMn11O24, Li8ZrMn11(NiO8)4 and Li4Mn4SiP3O16. All three candidates passed every filter, with Li6TiMn11O24 showing 3.85 V, 574 Wh/kg and energy above the hull 0.01 eV per atom, Li8ZrMn11(NiO8)4 showing 4.72 V, 676 Wh/kg and energy above the hull 0.02 eV per atom, and Li4Mn4SiP3O16 showing 3.92 V, 674 Wh/kg and energy above the hull 0.03 eV per atom. The agent concluded Ti and Ni dilutions give higher energy density than Zr and Al on the Ni-Mn spinel and Si-doped Mn-olivine is promising, and will prioritize dilute Ti/Ni variants on the Ni-Mn spinel and Si-doped Mn-olivine while avoiding Zr and Al dilution.
summaries.label: iteration 3

summaries.text: The agent searched for cobalt-free cathode candidates with higher energy density than LiFePO4 and proposed nine new compositions. Seven of them passed the initial stability funnel. The three most stable finalists were Li8TiMn11(NiO8)4 with energy above the hull of about 0.00 eV per atom, Li8Mn11V(NiO8)4 with about 0.01 eV per atom, and Li8ZrMn11(NiO8)4 with about 0.02 eV per atom. No band gap or energy density values were reported for the finalists in this run, so a comparative assessment versus LiFePO4 could not be completed. The run stopped after the planned iterations with stable candidates identified but without confirmed electronic or performance metrics.
